items.stem: Why can Snowflake scale query compute up and down without affecting stored data?

options.text: Storage and compute are separate layers, so virtual warehouses can resize independently of the data they read
options.rationale: Correct: Snowflake decouples storage from compute, letting warehouses scale on their own.

options.text: Every warehouse keeps its own private copy of all the data
options.rationale: Warehouses read from shared storage; they do not each copy all data.

options.text: Scaling compute automatically deletes unused tables
options.rationale: Resizing compute does not alter stored data.

options.text: Compute scaling only works if the tables are temporary
options.rationale: Scaling is independent of table type.

items.explanation: Correct: Snowflake decouples storage from compute, letting warehouses scale on their own.

items.stem: Which statements about Snowflake access control and governance are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Privileges are typically granted to roles, which are then granted to users
options.rationale: Correct: Snowflake uses role-based access control with a role hierarchy.

options.text: A masking policy can hide a column's value from users who lack the required role
options.rationale: Correct: dynamic data masking returns masked values based on the querying role.

options.text: Resource monitors change the schema of governed tables
options.rationale: Resource monitors track and cap credit usage; they do not alter schemas.

options.text: Granting privileges directly to each user is the recommended default
options.rationale: The recommended model grants through roles, not directly to users.

items.explanation: Correct: Snowflake uses role-based access control with a role hierarchy.; Correct: dynamic data masking returns masked values based on the querying role.
items.domain_ref: Security: roles, access control and masking

items.stem: A table was dropped by mistake an hour ago. What Snowflake feature recovers it most directly?

options.text: Time Travel, which can restore the table to a point within its retention window with UNDROP
options.rationale: Correct: Time Travel lets you UNDROP or query a table as of an earlier time within retention.
Auto-suspend manages compute cost, not data recovery.
Resource monitors track spend, not data history.
Masking controls visibility of values, not recovery of dropped objects.

items.explanation: Correct: Time Travel lets you UNDROP or query a table as of an earlier time within retention.
